name: Bruneian Empire
summary: A Malay sultanate on Borneo whose influence, after Melaka fell in 1511, stretched along the coasts of Borneo and into the Philippines, before it became a British protectorate in 1888.

location.value: Northern Borneo, with influence over the coasts of Borneo and the southern Philippines.

terrain.value: Coastal rivers, mangroves and rainforest of northern Borneo.

climate.value: Equatorial: hot and wet all year.

resources.value: Camphor, sago, forest products and pearls.

disasters.value: No major natural disasters are recorded; fires in the water villages.

population.value: No reliable estimate; Kampong Ayer was described by visitors in 1521 as a large water town.

urbanisation.value: Kampong Ayer, a town on stilts over the Brunei River, became the capital in 1660.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Sultanate of Brunei (1368–1888) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Saunders, A History of Brunei (2002)

disease.value: Smallpox and cholera in the 19th century.

migration.value: Chinese, Malay and Bornean traders and settlers.

economicBase.value: Trade and the collection of forest and sea products.

tradeRoutes.value: Trade with China, Melaka, Java and the Philippines.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Barter, cowries, piloncitos (small gold pieces) and later Brunei pitis coins.

inequality.value: Sultan and nobles (pengiran) above commoners and slaves.

governmentType.value: A Malay sultanate, with the sultan as head of state and religion.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Sultanate of Brunei (1368–1888) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Saunders, A History of Brunei (2002)

keyRulers.value: Muhammad Shah (founder), Sharif Ali, Bolkiah (1485–1524), Muhammad Hassan, Hashim Jalilul Alam.

succession.value: Hereditary in the royal family, often disputed.

institutions.value: Viziers (wazir) who ran the government, and Islamic law.

stability.value: A civil war (1660–1673) weakened the sultanate.

eliteConflict.value: A civil war between rival claimants to the throne (1660–1673).

armyAndTech.value: War boats and bronze swivel cannon (lantaka).

territoryChange.value: Lost Sarawak to James Brooke (from 1841) and Sabah to the British North Borneo Company.

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals included Spain, Sulu and later the British Raja of Sarawak.

inventions.value: Skilled bronze-casting of cannons and gongs.

scienceEducation.value: Islamic learning in mosques and the court.

openness.value: Open to Chinese, Malay and Arab traders.

communicationTransport.value: Boats on rivers and the sea; a trading fleet across Borneo and the Philippines.

religion.value: Sunni Islam, adopted by the rulers around the 15th century.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Sultanate of Brunei (1368–1888) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Saunders, A History of Brunei (2002)

languageWriting.value: Brunei Malay written in Jawi script; Arabic for religion.

artsArchitecture.value: Water villages on stilts (Kampong Ayer) and brassware.

dailyLife.value: Houses on stilts over the water at Kampong Ayer; rice, sago, fish.

ideasReligions.value: Spread Islam in Borneo and the Philippines.

colonisation.value: Lost most of its land to Sarawak and North Borneo; a British protectorate from 1888.

riseSignals.value: Expansion after Melaka fell to the Portuguese in 1511.

peakPeriod.value: Under Sultan Bolkiah (1485–1524), when its influence reached Manila.

declineSignals.value: Civil war and the loss of territory to Sarawak and North Borneo.

outcome.value: Became a British protectorate in 1888; independent again in 1984.

sources.value: Malay annals, Spanish records. Checked against Wikipedia (“Sultanate of Brunei (1368–1888)”).

knownFor.label: Kampong Ayer water village
knownFor.note: A town on stilts over the Brunei River.

knownFor.label: Lantaka bronze cannon
knownFor.note: Small swivel cannon used on boats.
